title: Retirement Plans: Identifying Ways to Help Mitigate Employer Risks Is Key to Continuing Defined Benefit Plans
summary:
What GAO Found

Defined Benefit (DB) plan coverage has declined over the last nearly 5 decades. In 1975, about 27 percent of private-sector workers participated in a single-employer DB plan. By 2023, that number had decreased to about 5 percent. Stakeholders cited a complex range of factors that contributed to this decline including increased costs, financial volatility for employers, and changes in the labor market, such as the decline of unions that often negotiated for DB benefits.

title: Science & Tech Spotlight: AI Chatbots and Mental Health
summary:
Why This Matters

Nearly one-fifth of Americans aged 12 to 21 reported using an AI chatbot for mental health advice in 2025. Experts warn that general-purpose chatbots are not designed for such needs and can be dangerous if used for this purpose. Further, while purpose-built chatbots may be designed to help, they are not a replacement for qualified mental health providers.

title: Science & Tech Spotlight: New World Screwworm Eradication
summary:
Why This Matters

New World screwworm is a parasitic fly that could cost the U.S. cattle industry billions of dollars per year. The eggs laid by screwworm flies hatch into larvae that infect cattle, sheep, and other animals, causing painful wounds and death if untreated. Over 100 total cases have been identified in the U.S. as of November 2026. Experts are concerned that existing control capabilities, which use sterile flies, may be insufficient to combat new outbreaks.
